claims.statement: Tom Allen issued a boasting challenge that he could whip any man in the world, and Jem Mace accepted it.
In 1869 Tom Allen issued a challenge to Bill McCoole.
After the Davis fight, a match was made between Charlie Gallagher and Tom Allen (or Tom Kelly) for $500 or $2,000 a side, to come off in five weeks.
Tom Allen said he would fight any man in the country who disputed his claim, for any purse that the challenger named.
After the fight Tom Allen challenged Charles Gallagher to fight him in five weeks for $1,000.
A $50 forfeit was put up for a fight within five weeks for $500 a side between Charles Gallagher and Tom Allen or Tom Kelley.
Gallagher's backer said Gallagher would fight either Tom Allen or Tom Kelley.
Tom Allen and Charles C. Gallagher had the preliminaries of a prize fight arranged and articles drawn up.
A $200 a side forfeit deposit was made for the Allen-Gallagher fight.
According to Tom Kehoe's testimony, Allen and his agent came the next day with $1,000 to back the Gallagher fight.
Tom Allen and Charlie Gallagher had the articles of agreement read and a final $300 a side deposit made with stakeholder William Murray.
After Allen revived, there was some talk of his rechallenging Charlie Gallagher for $5,000 a side, but nothing definite was arranged.
Tom Allen said he would re-meet Charley Gallagher in the ring within a week to a month for $1,000 to $5,000, but was no bar-room fighter.
The Allen-Gallagher fight was set for 23 February 1869.
Tom Allen challenged Charles A. Fong, presumably Gallagher, to a London Prize Ring fight for $1,000 a side one week later, leaving $250 as a first deposit at Campbell's saloon.
Tom Allen and Jack Looney called at the paper's office and said Gallagher refused a rematch that Looney had tried to arrange at Hennessey's saloon.
After the fight Tom Allen said he would fight Gallagher again immediately, or in a week, for any amount.
Jack Looney offered $1,500 to $1,200 that Tom Allen could whip Charley Gallagher in another tussle.
At McCoole's, Charley Gallagher agreed to an immediate rematch with Tom Allen in the ring.
A forfeit was put up by one of Tom Allen's admirers for a $1,000 match.
At a benefit exhibition at Looney's Hall, Tom Allen announced he was ready to meet Gallagher at any time.
Charley Gallagher had said he would accept Tom Allen's published challenge.
A fight between Charley Gallagher and Tom Allen was in contemplation in February 1869 and did not come off.
Tom Allen kept demanding another fight, saying he was able and willing to fight any man in America.
Mike McCoole then agreed to fight Tom Allen for any amount from $1,000 to $10,000.
Tom Allen challenged Mike McCoole to fight on McCoole's own ground for $2,500 a side within three months, with the money ready at William Carroll's, 510 Market Street.
Tom Allen said this was the second time Mike McCoole had been matched to fight him and had backed out.
On Saturday evening at a Chestnut Street saloon, Tom Allen said Mike McCoole could not whip him in an hour and a half.
A $1,000 wager was made, and a $50 forfeit put up by McCoole's friend was covered by Tom Allen.
Tom Allen said he had been matched to fight Mike McCoole on 6 March 1869.
Mike McCoole and Tom Allen agreed at Alex. McKee's to withdraw the stakes on their match and postpone the battle.
At the Broad Gauge saloon, McCoole refused to fight for the $500 balance of the deposit and insisted on $3,000 against $2,500, according to Allen.
Mike McCoole readily expressed willingness to accept Tom Allen's challenge.
Billy Carroll proposed a match for $2,500 a side, to be fought under London prize ring rules.
Mike McCoole readily agreed to the articles and was ready to put up money.
Allen was represented at the meeting by Billy Carroll and a second man whose surname is unreadable.
Patsy Reardon challenged Tom Allen in a city paper to a bout in the twenty-four foot arena.
Tom Allen answered Patsy Reardon's challenge with a counter-challenge to Reardon, or any other man, with provisos.
Tom Allen agreed to the long delay so that Mike McCoole could train, as McCoole was far from fighting condition.
Tom Allen and Mike McCoole drew up articles on 16 April 1869 at the Broad Gauge saloon for a fight within fifty miles of St. Louis, for $1,000 a side plus the excursion money.
In May 1869 Tom Allen and Mike McCoole signed articles for a London prize ring fight for $1,000 a side, to be fought on 15 June 1869.
Charley Gallagher challenged the winner of the McCool fight; Allen said he would accept, and the match was set for Chouteau's Island two months later.
Tom Allen said any future match with McCoole must be at least 200 miles from St. Louis.
Allen did not accept McCoole's challenge; he said he would fight for $5,000 a side but not inside 399 miles of St. Louis (printed as 399).
Allen is said to have put up a $1,000 forfeit at the St. Louis Billiard Hall.
Allen refused to fight McCoole again near St. Louis, because he did not believe he could get fair play there.
Allen offered to fight McCoole about three hundred miles east, in Kentucky, for $5,000 or more, with six friends each.
Allen offered to fight Charlie Gallagher at any place a respectable distance from St. Louis, wagering $2,500 to $1,500 on himself (printed as 61,500).
Allen wanted the Clipper or Wilkes' Spirit as stakeholder for any match.
Tom Allen had an appointment to meet Mike McCoole to make arrangements for another fight, but did not come.
After the McCool draw, Tom Allen said he would meet Charley Gallagher in 10 minutes; the meeting was fixed for August 17, 1869.
Mike McCoole published a challenge to Allen to fight again within three months, 50 to 100 miles from St. Louis, with money deposited at 298 North Third Street (printed as 298; OCR is poor).
McCoole offered, if Allen preferred, to fight him privately in a room before a few friends (text garbled).
Certain parties were working to bring about a renewal of the fight between Tom Allen and Mike McCoole, which the paper hoped would be postponed.
Charlie Gallagher challenged Tom Allen again a few days after the McCoole fight.
Tom Allen said he was willing to fight any man in America for a purse of $1,000 to $5,000.
Tom Allen offered to put up $2,500 against Charley Gallagher's $1,500 for a rematch.
Tom Allen wants his fight with Charley Gallagher to take place within fifty miles of Cincinnati.

Ben Hogan of Titusville, Pennsylvania, challenged Tom Allen to a prize fight under London prize ring rules for $1,000 and the boat money, to take place in Canada West three months after articles are signed.
Tom Allen deposited $200 with Mr. Carroll for a match with any man, and challenged Charley Gallagher to cover that deposit.
